meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common-law heritage; federal-provincial dual-sovereignty framework; the Province of British Columbia is exclusively common-law within a bijural federation)

Canada-United States Income Tax Convention (1980), as amended by the Fifth Protocol (2007), including the unlimited liability corporation (ULC) classification protocol

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 83.01-83.33 (terrorist financing); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 21; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (photo page) of each director and shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for documents originating in a Convention state; otherwise consular legalization at a Canadian embassy/consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each individual (utility bill or bank statement dated within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the jurisdiction of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if non-Convention origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if non-Convention origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for registered-office representation and service of process in British Columbia
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public (BC notary or origin-jurisdiction notary with apostille)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Consent to Act as Director, including personal information required for the BC Transparency Register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization only; Hague Apostille required if executed outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO / Transparency Register attestation and bank-account due-diligence questionnaire, including PEP declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant entity and founding legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization; Hague Apostille for counterparts executed abroad

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, officer and significant individual (25% or more ownership/control) against the FINTRAC List of Terrorists under Criminal Code s. 83.05, the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (Special Economic Measures Act), UN Security Council consolidated lists (United Nations Act), OFAC SDN and 50% Rule lists, and the UK HMT Consolidated List. PEP identification and close-associate screening are mandatory on a risk-based basis as defined under FINTRAC guidance for reporting entities. The payment rails (Stripe Billing, Paddle) will independently apply KYC/AML and acceptable-use underwriting. The ULC must implement and retain a written compliance program and keep all screening and KYC records for at least five years after the business relationship ends (PCMLTFA record-keeping requirements).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online, British Columbia Corporate Registry (Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia) - https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Roman alphabetic characters; English and/or French are permitted (French accents accepted by the registry). Non-Roman scripts must be transliterated into Roman letters. A BC unlimited liability company must end with the prescribed legal element 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company' (or the French 'SRI' / 'Societe a responsabilite illimitee') per BCBCA s. 24 and B.C. Reg. 202/2004. The proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing BC company names, extraprovincial registered names, and reserved names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: bank / banker / trust / trust company / loan company (Financial Institutions Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 141)
university / college / institute (Universities Act; Degree Authorization Act; College and Institute Act)
engineer / professional engineer / geoscientist / architect (professional regulatory statutes)
lawyer / barrister / solicitor / notary public (restricted legal professions)
royal / crown / government / municipal (implied Crown or governmental connection)
Canada / Canadian (requires federal charter or Global Affairs Canada name policy consent)
words implying a business activity that the company will not lawfully carry on
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A BC name reservation is valid for 56 days and may be renewed once for an additional 56 days (CAD $30 renewal fee via Corporate Online; renewal must be requested before expiry, otherwise a new reservation and fee are required). On rejection, the applicant may: (1) file a name-reconsideration request on Corporate Online within 30 days of the refusal (CAD $30 fee), attaching a written submission distinguishing the name from the cited conflicts; (2) resubmit a new name-reservation request with a revised proposed name; and (3) if administrative reconsideration is unsuccessful, apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review within 60 days of the final refusal under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241. The incorporation application and Notice of Articles must be filed before the name-reservation window closes.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. BCBCA s. 50 requires a registered office located in British Columbia at a physical civic street address (a P.O. Box alone is prohibited). A registered-agent or virtual-office provider is accepted by BC Registries and the CRA, provided the address is a physical location where documents and process can be served during normal business hours. For a no-code SaaS business (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210), a virtual registered office is commercially standard. However, Stripe Billing and Paddle conduct independent merchant underwriting and may require demonstrable operational substance (active website, domain ownership, management control, corporate bank account, and local business records) before activating merchant accounts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered office: approximately 15% probability of an unannounced verification visit within the first 36 months after incorporation (CRA GST/HST verification or BC Registrar compliance inspection). On-site business-premise inspection: below 10% for a remote-first, no-inventory, digitally delivered software service. CRA audits of software publishers are predominantly document-based (electronic records) rather than physical-premise-based.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and preliminary name reservation (Corporate Online)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee: CAD $30 per name reservation request

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reconsideration contingency (if the first name is rejected)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee: CAD $30 per reconsideration request

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation application (Notice of Articles, Notice of Registered Office, Notice of Directors, and ULC Articles of Incorporation)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, sections 10 (incorporation application), 11 (certificate of incorporation), and 51 (unlimited liability company status)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) together with Notice of Articles, Articles of Incorporation, and Incorporation Agreement
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement; shares may be issued for any consideration authorized by the board and disclosed in the notices
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED, that the Corporation accept the subscription of [Subscriber Name] for 100 common unlimited shares at CAD 0.01 par value, and issue such shares upon payment. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation be established at [Registered Address], British Columbia, and that the Corporation's records office be located at the same address. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name A] be appointed President and Director, [Name B] be appointed Secretary and Director, each to serve until successors are elected. All officers are authorized to execute required filings and open a corporate bank account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry, Corporate Registry Division (online name request service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search to confirm availability. File a name reservation request online through the BC Registry. Ensure the proposed name includes the mandatory ULC suffix. Retain the name reservation certificate for use in the incorporation application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, resubmit with a revised secondary name proposal within 30 days; appeal the refusal through the BC Registry or amend the name to avoid conflict.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and File Incorporation Application and Governing Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Incorporation Application) and prepare the Notice of Articles, Articles of Incorporation, and Incorporation Agreement. Attach the name reservation certificate. Submit the package online via BC Registry or by courier, and pay the required incorporation fee. Verify all director, shareholder, and registered office information before submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected for formal defects, correct the designated fields and resubmit within the cure period stated by the Registrar; expedited correction does not require new fees if filed within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation. Review the certificate for exact legal name, incorporation date, and registered corporate number. Store the original certificate in the corporate records book and file a certified copy with the records office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error, submit a request to the Registrar for a certificate of correction together with evidence of the error; no new incorporation application is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Organizational Resolutions and Issue Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution to accept share subscriptions, appoint officers, establish bank signatories, and authorize the issuance of shares. Prepare and issue share certificates and record transfers in the register of members.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural defect is found in the resolutions or share issuance, pass a ratifying board resolution correcting the record; no court application is required for pure administrative defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax Accounts and Business Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and BC Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the federal business number registration with the CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN). Activate any required GST/HST account, payroll deduction account, and corporate income tax account. Register the ULC with the BC Ministry of Finance for provincial corporate tax and apply for any municipal business licence if a physical office is established.
required_dossiers: Directors' and officers' identification and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is incomplete, contact the CRA Business Registration helpdesk to amend the account onboarding within 30 days; penalties for late registration may be waived if a voluntary disclosure is filed before demand letters are issued.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – GST/HST, federal corporate income tax, and Business Number administration, through My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE; BC Ministry of Finance, Taxation and Revenue Administration – Provincial Sales Tax (PST), through eTaxBC (etax.gov.bc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the BC ULC under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act. 2) Apply to CRA for a Business Number (BN) and a GST/HST account via Business Registration Online or CRA My Business Account; provide ULC registration details, Canadian registered/head office address, expected revenue bands, ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 activity description, and corporate constituent documents. 3) For taxable sales of software or digital services to BC customers, register with the BC Ministry of Finance for PST via eTaxBC after obtaining the BN; provide BN, legal entity status, and BC sales description. 4) If the ULC is foreign-owned and supplies digital products to Canadian consumers, use CRA's non-resident simplified GST/HST registration where eligible, and maintain target payment rails (Stripe Billing, Paddle) metadata for tax reporting. 5) Retain CRA registration letter, BN/RT account confirmation, and eTaxBC enrolment reference as statutory identity evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: For Canadian domestic income tax, a BC ULC is a resident corporation subject to entity-level taxation under the Income Tax Act; there is no domestic Canadian check-the-box election. For United States federal tax purposes, a Canadian ULC wholly or majority owned by a U.S. person is eligible to check the box under Treasury Regulation §301.7701-3 to be classified as a disregarded entity (single-member) or a partnership (multi-member), producing pass-through treatment in the United States. Such divergent classification creates hybrid entity status and triggers OECD BEPS Action 2 / hybrid mismatch rules, Canadian GAAR, and reporting obligations under Part XVIII. Canada also permits certain deemed-status or fair-value elections in connection with foreign affiliate and cross-border transactions, but these do not alter the fundamental domestic corporate tax treatment of the ULC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) and British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST); no Harmonized Sales Tax in BC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies in a calendar quarter and over the preceding four calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold; non-resident remote digital suppliers also use CAD 30,000). BC PST: CAD 10,000 of taxable sales to customers in British Columbia in a calendar year (PST small-seller threshold); once exceeded, a non-resident or remote vendor must register and collect BC PST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control e-invoicing, API pre-authorization, or digital stamping at the federal level. CRA accepts electronic invoices and records if they are complete, legible, and retained in a reproducible format. GST/HST registrants must remit returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or CRA-certified software. BC PST registrants must file and remit through eTaxBC. Voluntary PEPPOL-compliant e-invoicing is available but not legally mandated. No pre-clearance or stamping requirement applies before issuing an invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, supplies are zero-rated when: (i) physical goods are exported from Canada by the supplier or for the supplier and satisfy the documentary evidence requirements; (ii) services are supplied to a non-resident recipient, provided the service is not performed in respect of Canadian real property, not rendered to an individual physically in Canada, and not directly connected to Canadian tangible personal property; and (iii) intangible personal property, including SaaS and digital no-code website-builder subscriptions, is supplied to a non-resident and the evidence establishes the non-resident status of the recipient and the foreign place of use or receipt. Digital subscription services delivered online to non-resident customers on platforms such as Stripe Billing and Paddle generally qualify as zero-rated exports. BC PST does not apply to zero-rated exports of goods or to software delivered to non-residents outside BC.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CERS/B13A) for physical exported goods
Commercial Invoice describing the goods, digital service, or software licence
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for physical goods)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/SWIFT payment settlement evidence
Written contract or purchase order identifying the non-resident recipient
Non-resident status evidence, such as foreign tax identification number or passport/address proof
Delivery and usage logs for digital services, including subscriber IP addresses and server logs
GST/HST export record or self-declaration of export intent
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny a zero-rating claim where export substantiation is incomplete or the payment evidence is not retained within the prescribed documentary timeframe. A retroactive reassessment may impose uncollected GST/HST plus interest at prescribed rates. Penalties include administrative fines for false statements or omissions, gross-negligence penalties calculated with reference to the net tax misstatement, and, in serious cases, prosecution for wilful evasion. Where a ULC claims tax-free export status for internal digital services and fails to demonstrate non-resident receipt, CRA may impose a 25% or higher civil penalty on the understated tax, extend the normal four-year reassessment period to seven years for misrepresentation, and disallow input tax credits. The BC Ministry of Finance may claw back PST exemptions and charge interest and penalties on unremitted PST for non-compliant remote software vendors.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) and the Department of Finance Canada; foreign exchange administration in Canada is not centralized in a single control authority. The Currency Act, the Exchange Control Act (largely repealed), the Bank Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act govern cross-border currency and reporting. Operational oversight for banking and solvency is conducted by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), while market conduct in the securities and derivatives space falls under the Canadian Securities Administrators and the Bank of Canada for clearing and settlement system oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible with a fully open current account and capital account. There are no general exchange controls, capital controls, prior licenses, or approval requirements for foreign direct investment, shareholder equity injections, intercompany loans, dividend remittance, or profit repatriation. Convertibility is constrained only by standard AML/KYC requirements, FINTRAC cross-border reporting thresholds, FATCA/CRS self-certification, and ordinary banking due diligence. Profit remittance may be subject to Canadian Part XIII withholding tax on dividends, interest, rents, or royalties and to the Canada-US tax treaty if applicable; however, no central bank or exchange administration obstacle exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement for export proceeds, cross-border software licensing revenues, or SaaS subscription receipts. Exporters and service providers may retain foreign currency in offshore or onshore accounts and convert at their discretion. All incoming and outgoing wire transfers and EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more must be reported by banks, money service businesses, and authorized financial institutions under FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting rules. The ULC must therefore maintain full supporting commercial documentation for all cross-border receipts and disbursements to satisfy anti-money-laundering due diligence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to moderate for primary treasury purposes. Foreign fintech EMIs and digital banking platforms, including UK-style e-money institutions or U.S.-licensed digital banks, are not authorized to act as Canadian Schedule I or II banks and do not have direct membership in Payments Canada payment systems. They may be used as auxiliary collection or payout rails, but only if registered as a money services business with FINTRAC in Canada and compliant with the Retail Payment Activities Act once fully implemented. A ULC must maintain its core settlement and treasury accounts with a Canadian chartered bank to ensure LVTS clearing, SWIFT correspondent access, and full regulatory certainty. Use of EMIs is acceptable only for low-value subscription collection and contractor payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Major Canadian banks generally require at least one director or an authorized corporate officer to appear physically at a branch in Canada for the initial KYC interview, because corporate account opening demands verification of identity, signing authority, operating structure, and beneficial ownership under FINTRAC regulations. Hybrid remote opening is increasingly possible for companies with existing global banking relationships or using live video identification, but in practice the bank will require certified copies of the ULC formation documents, a current Certificate of Good Standing from the British Columbia Corporate Registry, the corporate resolution authorizing account opening, and notarized identity documents for all directors and 25% or greater shareholders. Board meetings and signatory resolutions should be passed in Canada or recognized under BC law. A fully remote process is not guaranteed and should not be assumed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited liability corporation with no public shareholder registry; the bank cannot independently verify ultimate beneficial ownership through public corporate filings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Register of Members; completed beneficial ownership declaration; certified corporate resolutions authorizing issuance of shares; share subscription agreements; notarized passports and proof of residential address for all directors and shareholders; a signed FATCA/CRS self-certification for every UBO; and a written explanation of the commercial purpose of the ULC and its no-code website builder business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border SaaS subscription inflows and simultaneous outbound disbursements to foreign contractors or marketing vendors, triggering live-entity review for possible trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer subscription agreements; Stripe and Paddle merchant settlement reports; IP assignment agreements; domain and infrastructure invoices; employee and contractor agreements; corporate books and client contracts demonstrating genuine operating activity; and a documented treasury policy distinguishing subscription revenue from capital injections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large non-resident capital injection from a related party into a newly formed ULC before any significant Canadian revenue stream, raising source-of-funds and round-tripping concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder loan or contribution agreement; board resolution approving the inbound transfer; source bank statements and wire confirmations from the remitting entity; financial statements or audited accounts of the shareholder; evidence of tax compliance in the shareholder's jurisdiction; and a liquidated business plan for the Canadian ULC including projected SaaS subscription revenue and host-country market rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential confusion over the ULC's hybrid tax treatment and US check-the-box pass-through status, causing the bank to flag inconsistent FATCA/CRS reporting by Canadian and non-resident owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Canadian law firm tax opinion on the ULC classification; IRS Form W-8BEN-E or Form W-9 as applicable; equivalent CRS forms for Canadian and foreign shareholders; shareholder-level tax identification numbers; the Canada-U.S. treaty eligibility analysis; and a corporate organizational chart showing the ULC's place within the group.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The ULC should maintain a CAD operational account and a USD operational account with a Schedule I Canadian bank to receive cross-border funding. Equity subscriptions and shareholder loans should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the parent or shareholder to the ULC's account, using the standard bank BIC; field 70 should identify the transaction as 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN' because Canada does not assign standard product purpose codes. The receiving bank will request the executed share subscription agreement, corporate resolution, board consent, source-of-funds confirmation, and FATCA/CRS self-certification before releasing funds into the operating account. Once cleared, funds are settled through Payments Canada LVTS for Canadian-dollar wires or through the respective USD clearing channel and the bank's internal ledger for US-dollar deposits. All transfers equal to or above CAD 10,000 are subject to FINTRAC electronic funds transfer reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade and service payments should be cleared using SWIFT MT103 for high-value and one-off vendor settlements, SWIFT MT202 for corporate-to-corporate treasury transfers, and through the bank's USD correspondent network via Fedwire or CHIPS where required. For larger supply contracts involving physical goods or commissioning, the ULC may use a commercial letter of credit or documentary collection through SWIFT MT700, with INCOTERMS embedded in the trade documentation. Domestic Canadian dollar disbursements may be cleared through Payments Canada ACSS and LVTS, and lower-value payments can be made via Interac e-Transfer, wire transfer API, or automated clearing entry. In every case, the ULC must retain purchase orders, invoices, delivery evidence, and proof of payment to satisfy FINTRAC and bank due diligence requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with an authorized Canadian bank or swap dealer
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid currencies when the underlying commercial obligation supports the hedge
Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps for treasury balance-sheet hedging
Plain vanilla FX options and FX collars
Single-currency and cross-currency interest rate swaps where permitted under the Bank Act and applicable derivatives regulation
FX forwards embedded in commercial cross-border loan agreements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report for Unlimited Liability Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies / BC Registries and Online Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two calendar months after every anniversary of incorporation; for example, an entity incorporated on 15 March must file by 14 May each year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late fee is charged if the annual report is filed after the two-month window; continued failure to file allows the Registrar, after statutory notice, to administratively strike the ULC off the register. Strike-off causes loss of corporate capacity until restoration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal Part I and BC provincial corporate income tax under the single filing agreement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the end of the corporate taxation year; for a calendar-year taxpayer, by June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month of delinquency (maximum 12 months); repeated or gross-negligent failure may trigger additional penalty assessments and prosecution, and unpaid statutory withholdings may attract director liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The BC Business Corporations Act does not impose an audit threshold based on revenue, assets or employees for a non-reporting private ULC. An independent audit is compulsory only if the ULC is a reporting issuer under securities law, is directed by shareholder resolution or its articles, is subject to a sectoral regulator requiring audited financial statements, or is obligated by a lending/investment agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Part II) is permitted for a private non-reporting BC ULC. An outbound SaaS no-code builder will normally use ASPE unless consolidated by a public parent or required by investors to adopt IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Canada/BC do not require a public UBO filing with the annual report. Under the BC Business Corporations Act transparency-register regime, the private ULC must maintain a Transparency Register of significant individuals (beneficial owners and controlling directors). The register must be updated within the prescribed period after any transfer of shares or change of significant control, must be produced to enforcement officers and the Registrar on demand, and should be internally validated each year before the BC Annual Report is submitted. The BC Annual Report itself only confirms the registered office, mailing address, directors and officers; it does not contain shareholding or UBO details.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Central Securities Register and Register of Transfers
Minute Book (directors' and shareholders' minutes and resolutions, with consents to act)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$260–US$600 per year (CAD$350–CAD$800) for a BC registered office and corporate secretarial agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No mandatory audit. If engaged voluntarily or by covenant: US$5,000–US$12,000 for a review engagement and US$15,000–US$40,000 for a full audit of a low-risk SaaS/no-code platform with standard recurring revenue.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined for general corporations (15% federal base rate + 12% British Columbia general corporate income tax rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday. Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) may claim the Small Business Deduction on up to C$500,000 of active business income, resulting in an 11% combined rate (9% federal + 2% BC), but a foreign-controlled ULC normally does not qualify. Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits (refundable or non-refundable) are available for qualifying software and low-code platform R&D.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed electronically through CRA-approved EFILE service providers or the CRA's online portal (NETFILE for T2). The T2 includes the BC provincial corporate tax computation (Schedules 4 and 5) because BC operates under a tax collection agreement with the CRA.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period must be 12 months or less; instalment payments are required quarterly if tax payable exceeds C$3,000)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for December 31 year-end). The balance-due day is 2 months after the year-end (3 months for CCPCs), with interest accruing on any late payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter federal BN and BC incorporation number; identify as an Unlimited Liability Corporation (BC/AB) and disclose ownership by non-resident shareholders.
Report worldwide revenue and expense in Canadian dollars; attach financial statements and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for cross-border transactions with non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after losses and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply non-capital loss carryforwards only to the extent permitted (20 years); do not claim CCPC small-business deductions unless the ULC is Canadian-controlled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provincial corporation tax computation for British Columbia
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate taxable income to BC allocable permanent establishments; apply the 12% BC general rate; no small-business rate unless CCPC status is valid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax attributes, unused losses, and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Track capital and non-capital loss balances; document any fines or interest connected to non-resident payments to ensure deductibility under section 67.5.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 5% of the unpaid tax when filing is past due, plus 1% per full month of arrears for up to 12 months (10% maximum add-on). A repeated failure on the same return triggers a 10% late-filing penalty. Gross-negligence penalties may reach 50% of the misreported amount, and criminal tax evasion fines can be 50% to 200% of the evaded tax plus imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) for dividends paid to non-resident shareholders from the ULC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must complete CRA Form NR301 (treaty-based exemption or reduction) and provide a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the relevant foreign tax authority. The withholding agent must retain the completed form and TRC as supporting evidence. Under the Canada-US DTA, treaty rates for dividends are 5% (where the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of voting shares) and 15% for portfolio shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII withholding is 25% for royalties and interest paid to non-residents, subject to exemptions and treaties. Arm's-length interest is exempt under s. 212(1)(b). Royalties under the Canada-US DTA are generally reduced to 10% (or 0% for certain copyright royalties); interest is typically 0% for arm's-length debt and 15% for excessive interest.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is required where the aggregate fair market value of non-arm's-length cross-border transactions exceeds C$1,000,000 per year. A Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding C$750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate Economic Substance Regulations in the Caribbean/ESR sense, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245) and transfer-pricing provisions (s. 247) impose a genuine economic-substance standard. A ULC that exists solely as a tax-transparent shell, with no Canadian office, employees, or business functions, is exposed to CRA recharacterization, treaty-benefit denial, and reassessment with interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting income from Canadian online subscriptions, fabricating expenses, or providing false records to the CRA for the no-code website builder business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under s. 239 ITA carries a fine between 50% and 200% of the tax evaded and up to 5 years imprisonment. Civil gross negligence penalty under s. 163(2) is 50% of the understated tax plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who authorized false statements can be criminally prosecuted and personally fined. Under BC ULC statutes, shareholders have unlimited liability for the company's obligations, including federal tax debts, when the corporation is unable to pay.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany management fees or IP royalties for software code in a manner inconsistent with the arm's length principle, or failing to prepare contemporaneous documentation once the C$1 million threshold is crossed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may reprice the transaction under s. 247, assess additional tax plus arrears interest, and impose a penalty equal to 10% of the reassessment amount (the greater of C$5,000 or 10% of the adjustment).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for TP penalties, but if the mispricing amounts to negligence or willful blindness, directors can be held jointly and severally liable under the federal Income Tax Act for source deduction failures and, in BC, under the ULC unlimited liability regime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a BC ULC as a conduit for US to reinvested software royalties without Canadian economic substance, employees, or business activity, solely to benefit from U.S.-Canada treaty withholding reductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA can invoke GAAR (s. 245) to deny the treaty benefit and re-dissect the transaction, resulting in full Part XIII withholding (25%), accumulated interest, and a 50% misrepresentation penalty where falsified documentation exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors remain exposed to non-compliance under the BC B.C. Unlimited Liability Company Act; the unlimited liability of shareholders and directors is not capped where corporate formalities are ignored and personal guarantees or nominee arrangements veil the reality of control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file BC annual reports, maintain a registered office in BC, or register the ULC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act if the entity is treated as a money-services business; accepting anonymous or high-risk crypto or wire payments from undetermined sources for the no-code platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: BC Registrar can dissolve the ULC for non-filing; failure to comply with AML obligations can result in administrative monetary penalties up to C$10 million for repeated corporate non-compliance, and criminal fines for directors and officers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A dissolved ULC exposes shareholders to joint personal liability for liabilities incurred after dissolution. Directors who knowingly allow the company to be used for laundering proceeds face forfeiture of assets, travel bans, and imprisonment under the Criminal Code of Canada (s. 462.31).
